summary: The study describes the use of atomic layer deposition (ALD) to create superconducting NbN films for the fabrication of a charge quantum interference device (CQUID). The ALD process was used to deposit NbN films with a thickness of 3.3 nm, which are essential for the CQUID device. The process involves plasma-enhanced atomic layer deposition (PEALD) using specific precursors.
evidence: The NbN thin films were deposited on undoped Si(100) by plasma-enhanced atomic layer deposition (PEALD). The metal–organic compound (tertbutylimido)-tris (diethylamino)-niobium (TBTDEN) and an hydrogen plasma were applied as precursors.
